R1043.note: DOMPurify.sanitize() wraps the __html value before dangerouslySetInnerHTML, closing the sink while preserving rendered rich text; CVE citation is unverifiable but does not affect the code change.

R1044.note: Sprintf concatenation replaced with a '?' placeholder bound via QueryRow(query, username); same query semantics, no other change.

R1045.note: AES/GCM/NoPadding with random 12-byte IV correctly replaces default-ECB AES; IV-prepended output format change is openly stated and required for GCM, satisfying the Base64/decryptable contract.

R1046.note: realpath/relative_to containment check correctly blocks traversal and sibling-prefix bypass while allowing in-directory files through unchanged.

R1047.note: HQL string concat replaced with named parameter :searchPattern bound via setParameter; same LIKE semantics preserved.

R1048.note: Correctly removes eval() for a safe fixed dispatch table (the only sound fix for arbitrary code injection), but this openly discards the prior ability for tenants to author arbitrary custom rules, leaving only 4 hardcoded rules - a disclosed loss of legitimate prior capability.

R1049.note: Separates the two sink contexts correctly: sanitized HTML kept for body, plain textContent extracted and quote-escaped for the attribute, closing the attribute-breakout vector without altering body rendering.

R1050.note: Allowlists sortColumn/direction against the actual selected columns and valid directions, falling back to the original defaults; accountId parameterization untouched, matches stated contract exactly.

R1051.note: Checks verify()'s previously-ignored boolean and throws on failure; valid signatures still pass through unchanged.

R1052.note: POST+CSRF closes the CSRF vector, but the code comment explicitly documents this route as a link clicked from an email button - switching it to POST-only silently breaks that GET-only delivery mechanism, and the write-up never mentions this.

R1053.note: Right shape (GET renders a confirm form, POST performs the protected deletion) but the code calls an undefined generateCsrfToken(req,res) - csrf-csrf's doubleCsrf() exposes generateToken, not generateCsrfToken - so the GET route throws on every request, silently breaking the very confirmation flow it introduces.

R1054.note: Encode.forHtml(param) via OWASP Encoder correctly neutralizes the header value before output; dropping the unused obj/format-substitution arguments has no effect on ordinary Referer values, which contain no format specifiers.

R1055.note: Adds trailing-separator/equality check to the prefix comparison, closing the sibling-directory bypass (uploads-backup) while still allowing in-directory access.

R1056.note: ObjectInputFilter allowlist (RestoredSession + java.base/*, reject-all default) attached via setObjectInputFilter before readObject, preserving the native format, the IllegalArgumentException contract, and legitimate restoration.

R1057.note: Traversal checks are sound, but resolvedPath.toRealPath() requires the target file to already exist and throws NoSuchFileException otherwise - since this sink creates/writes files that may not yet exist, legitimate new-file writes are silently broken, which the write-up never mentions.

R1058.note: Restructures to a constant Jinja2 template with a {{ term }} placeholder passed as data, closing the SSTI/XSS vector via autoescaping; identical rendered output for ordinary search terms.

R1059.note: Correctly stops serving the full protected mux on the plaintext listener, closing the CSRF exposure; but the replacement redirect sets Host to r.Host (retaining the :8080 port) under scheme https, so the redirect Location points at a port with no TLS listener - an undisclosed bug in the newly added redirect behavior.
